acceptance.test: Claude managed hooks are exactly SessionStart and PostCompact; a legacy issueops hook co-resident with a third-party hook on the same managed event is removed while the third-party hook survives
acceptance.observed: The pre-seed home/.claude/settings.json (saved verbatim to settings-preseed-round3.txt, sha256 5d8a302fb69e0f76150247cca67e67496209d20cf1e9eae176b0d0e6f039731d) held 5 events: SessionStart with TWO co-resident groups -- a legacy issueops group ('/private/tmp/issueops-lane-456-legacy/bin/issueops' hook session-start) and a third-party group (third-party-session-tool --warm-cache); PostCompact (issueops managed, unseeded); PreToolUse (third-party-lint-tool --check only); UserPromptSubmit (legacy issueops group only); Stop with two co-resident groups (legacy issueops + third-party-notify-tool --stop). After the install run, the post-merge file (saved verbatim to settings-postmerge-round3.txt, sha256 42658087e1d784f68d53c5cd0ffb1206bb38d5e4fbf9430e06956189510cc0b1, independently re-parsed as valid JSON with python3 -m json.tool) has exactly 4 event keys. SessionStart -- the highest-risk case because it is a managed event -- now holds exactly two groups: the surviving third-party-session-tool group plus the newly appended '/private/tmp/issueops-lane-456/source/bin/issueops' hook session-start --host claude group; the legacy issueops SessionStart group is gone. PostCompact is unchanged (still the sole issueops managed group). PreToolUse still holds only the untouched third-party-lint-tool group. Stop now holds only the surviving third-party-notify-tool group; its co-resident legacy issueops group was removed by the same pass. UserPromptSubmit is absent entirely: its only group was the legacy issueops hook, so the event emptied out and the installer deleted the key. This exercises internal/adapter/claude/install_hooks.go's mergeClaudeHookConfig/HookGroupContainsAgentHarness against real upgrade-over-existing-config input, including the specific co-residency-on-a-managed-event case, and proves both halves of AC-04 with a byte-diffable before/after pair rather than the post-state alone.
